cultural.vision_reason: This is a strip-woven cotton robe (boubou/riga/tobe) with embroidered pocket and front panel, a classic Muslim West African men's gown style worn by Wolof and neighboring Sahelian peoples alike; the garment type is plausible for the claimed group even if the specific "aska biyu" motif name is Hausa-derived.

physical.title: gown
physical.summary: Man's gown (tobe, boubou, riga). The body is composed of 116 narrow strips of hand-spun white cotton hand-sewn together along the edges. The strips in the tunic are sewn vertically, while those of the sleeves are sewn horizontally and are of uneven length so that they flare out towards the top. A square pocket has been sewn onto the front of the tunic. The pocket, shoulder and front are hand-embroidered in green imported cotton thread with the 'two knives' pattern (aska biyu) in satin and buttonhole eyelet stitch. The tunic is hemmed around the neck, sleeves and base. The base is also lined with a broad strip of plain woven cotton composed of alternating diagonal lines in purple (possibly alaari silk) and green and white cotton.
